messages.content: 我想在聖荷西附近的Walmart買蘋果、米飯和12罐瓶裝水。請顯示產品資訊和庫存情況。

function.name: walmart_purchase
function.description: Retrieve information of items from Walmart including stock availability. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

product_list.description: Items to be purchased listed in an array.

pack_size.description: Size of the product pack if applicable. The size of the array should be equal to product_list. Default is not use it if not specified.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to buy apples, rice, and 12 cans of bottled water at Walmart near San Jose. They want product info and inventory status. We need to call the function walmart_purchase with location "San Jose" or "near San Jose". Provide product list ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"] and pack sizes? For apples maybe no pack size; for rice maybe pack size? For bottled water we have 12 cans. So pack_size array should match product_list length. For apples and rice, we can set pack_size as null or omitted. But the function signature says pack_size?: number[]. It expects array of numbers equal to product_list length. If we don't specify pack_size, default is not used. But we might provide pack_size: [null, null, 12] but that may cause type mismatch. Better to omit pack_size entirely. But the function signature requires pack_size? optional. So we can just pass loc: "San Jose", product_list: ["apples", "rice", "bottled water"]. That should be fine.

We need to call the function.
